page: Amazon Web Services z1d.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8151 x86_64 processor delivering a sustained clock frequency of 4.0 GHz across 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 900 GB NVMe SSD, while network capacity provides a 12 Gbps baseline. The platform incorporates hardware extensions including AVX-512, AES, and FMA, with no discrete GPU accelerators present.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem throughput, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 25% at 2818.27 and uncached read bandwidth reaching 107.83 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks reflect solid mid-tier execution, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 9969.0, PassMark CPU of 25592.05, and single-threaded gzip compression of 28.23 GB/sec. In application-specific synthetic tests, the instance executed 24.54 million Redis SET operations per second and attained a Clang software compilation score of 21145.0. Workloads requiring large language model inference show clear limits, as 70B parameter prompt processing drops to 3.8 tokens/sec, falling into the bottom 10%.

The combination of high per-core clock speed and dense memory capacity yields high resource efficiency for environments tied to per-core enterprise software licensing. The integrated NVMe instance store delivers fast local scratch space, though non-persistent local disks require external replication strategies for durable persistence. The z1d.6xlarge is technically matched for relational database engines, Redis in-memory caches, electronic design automation (EDA), and high-frequency computational tasks requiring both memory density and rapid single-thread clock cycles.
